HOUSE + POOL DESIGN STUDIES

Palm Garden Long House

Five single-storey options, each built on the right side of the existing annex. View: standing at the gate, looking down the driveway to the annex door.

THE SITE, RECALIBRATED

Gate, driveway, annex, then the new house

The driveway runs along the short side of the land, straight from the gate to the annex door. Coming in, the boundary wall is on your left and the whole land is on your right.

Every option starts at the annex and runs along the north edge on its right side, facing south, so the lawn, the date palms and the hedges stay open in front of the new house.

All five repeat the annex’s river pebble, ochre render, clay-tile edge and arched timber openings.

Right: option B at night. Sizes are estimated from site photos.

OPTION A

Pebble Line

Extend the annex in one straight line

≈ 140 m² new

Pool 19 × 4 m lap · cost $

The house continues straight on from the annex along the north edge, with the same pebble base, ochre render and clay-tile edge. The raised middle room opens south through four arched glass doors to a terrace and a 19 m lap pool.

GAINS

— Joined to the annex: one continuous building

— The lawn stays open to the south

— Lowest cost, one-phase build

WATCH FOR

— A long façade needs the raised middle to avoid looking like a barracks

OPTION B

Riwaq Courtyard

A U-shaped house around a private pool

≈ 220 m² new

Pool 7 × 6 m · cost $$$

The back wing runs along the north edge beside the annex, with an arched riwaq (shaded loggia) in front. Two short wings frame a courtyard pool that opens south to the lawn.

GAINS

— Arches repeat the annex’s timber door

— The pool is sheltered on three sides

— Annex becomes the guest suite

WATCH FOR

— Largest floor area and highest cost

— Courtyard needs cross-ventilation in summer

OPTION C

Palm Pavilions

Three small houses joined by a timber walkway

≈ 140 m² new

Pool ≈ 95 m² free-form · cost $$

Three pavilions with clay-tile roofs step east from the annex along the north edge, linked by a covered timber walkway. A free-form pool curves across the lawn toward the date palms, 3 m clear of their trunks.

GAINS

— Build one pavilion at a time

— Scale stays close to the annex

— Every palm stays in place

WATCH FOR

— Moving between rooms means stepping outside

OPTION D

Hedge-Edge Modern

A flat-roofed glass bar against the north hedge

≈ 140 m² new

Pool 18 × 4 m mirror · cost $$

A thin roof slab floats over a glass wall facing south across the lawn. Pebble end walls tie it to the annex, and a timber screen covers the bedrooms. The whole lawn stays open.

GAINS

— Biggest open lawn of the five

— The north hedge forms the back wall

— Night reflections in the mirror pool

WATCH FOR

— The biggest stylistic step away from the annex

— Glass needs deep overhangs or low-E glazing

OPTION E

Vaulted Long House

Egyptian vernacular: vaults, a dome and a wind-catcher

≈ 140 m² + riwaq new

Pool 8 × 8 m birka + rill · cost $$

Barrel-vaulted rooms in the Hassan Fathy tradition, with a domed majlis at the centre and a malqaf wind-catcher at the far end. A square birka pool with a fountain sits on the dome’s axis, fed by a narrow rill.

GAINS

— Passive cooling from thick walls and the malqaf

— Ochre, pebble and arches carried through

— Strong local identity

WATCH FOR

— Vaults and domes need an experienced builder

— The pool is for cooling off, not swimming laps
